_documentation: Sample MCP-client config for ghostloop. Pick the block that matches your client (Claude Desktop / Cursor / Continue / Cline / Zed / Gemini CLI) and your OS. Replace /absolute/path/to/ghostloop with the real path. Restart the client after editing.

claude_desktop.Linux: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (unofficial; Claude Desktop on Linux is community-built)

_stdio_block_works_for_every_client: Claude Desktop, Cursor, Continue, Cline, Zed, and Gemini CLI all share the same { command, args, env } shape under their respective mcpServers / context_servers keys. The block below works for every single one — paste it into the right config file and restart the client.

mcpServers._remote_http_setup_for_mobile_or_remote_: Run the script directly on the host that owns the robot (NOT under the desktop client) so it stays up across desktop restarts. Then any remote / mobile MCP client connects via the URL — not the command/args path. Bind 0.0.0.0 only when you have authentication or a private network. Default 127.0.0.1 is safer.

_run_http_command_examples.macOS_Linux: GHOSTLOOP_BACKEND=mock GHOSTLOOP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http GHOSTLOOP_HOST=0.0.0.0 GHOSTLOOP_PORT=8765 python3 examples/claude_desktop_mcp_arm.py
_run_http_command_examples.Windows_cmd: set GHOSTLOOP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http && set GHOSTLOOP_HOST=0.0.0.0 && set GHOSTLOOP_PORT=8765 && python examples\claude_desktop_mcp_arm.py

ghostloop-remote-http._note: Use this URL form in MCP clients that support remote HTTP servers (Claude Desktop 0.8+, Cursor latest, mobile MCP clients). The robot host runs the script as shown above; clients just connect.
